chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Rifa'ah, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“If the ground is wet and there is in it neither dust nor water, then look for the driest place you can find and perform tayammum from it, for that is an easing from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

He said: “If he is in snow, then let him look to the felt of his saddle and perform tayammum from its dust, or from something dusty. And if he is in a condition where he finds nothing but clay, then there is no harm in performing tayammum from it.”

key_terms.تَوْسِيعٌ: an easing or facilitation granted by Allah
key_terms.ثَلْجٍ: snow, indicating a condition of severe cold or frozen surroundings
key_terms.غُبَارِهِ: its dust, meaning dust found on an object such as the saddle-felt
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمْ: perform tayammum, the dry ablution in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.مُبْتَلَّةً: soaked or wet, describing difficult terrain for ritual purification
key_terms.ٱلطِّينَ: clay or mud, allowed as a source for tayammum in necessity
key_terms.ٱلْأَرْضُ: the ground or earth used as the basis for tayammum

ai.seo_question: How should tayammum be performed when the ground is wet, snowy, or only clay is available?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the rulings of tayammum in difficult conditions when normal materials or water are not available. It shows the flexibility of the Sacred Law by permitting tayammum from the driest available ground, from dust on equipment, or even from clay when nothing else is found. The narration highlights divine ease in acts of ritual purity and worship.
